# Test scripts

A test script turns a process document into a manual test that can be run again, for example after a Business Central upgrade.

## Creating a run

**Run test** in a documentation card's menu in the document library builds the document the same way Word export does (`T9WordExportPipeline.createPresentation`), in the document language and with the user's edits, and takes the workflow steps from it (`src/document/test-script.js`). Bug reports and recordings in progress do not offer it. The run opens on its own page (`test-run.html`).

Each step keeps its number, the heading it is under and its instruction as the document reads. The expected result of a step starts from the verification notes written for it and is otherwise empty for the user to write; the recording's own observation of a step is not used, since it is generated text in one language and not a statement of what should happen. The process's expected result is shown when the user wrote one in the review.

## Running

The tester marks each step Passed, Failed, Skipped or Not run and can add a comment, a tester name and the environment tested. Every change is saved automatically with a visible state; a failed save keeps the changes on the page and offers a retry. The summary counts the results: the run has failed as soon as one step failed and has passed when every step passed or was skipped.

**Run again** starts a new run with the same steps and expected results and nothing tested. A run made later from the document takes the expected results written in the latest earlier run of the same document for steps that have none, matched by the step's identity in the document. Earlier runs of the document are listed with their results.

**Prerequisites** say what must be in place before the test starts. **Test data** names the values the steps work with, such as a customer or an item; an expected result can name a value as `{Name}` (matched without regard to case), and the page and the panel show the expected result with the values filled in. An unknown name is left as written. A run made later from the document takes the prerequisites and test data of the latest earlier run when it has none of its own. The panel shows both in a collapsible block above the step.

**Export** saves the run as Markdown or as a CSV file for Excel, in the document language, and reports it as saved only after the browser has written the file. The CSV file has one row per step with the expected result filled in, starts with a byte order mark so that Excel reads it as UTF-8, separates columns with a comma for an English document and a semicolon otherwise, and keeps a cell that would start a formula as text.

**Test protocol** opens the run as a page to print or save as PDF (`test-protocol.html`): the outcome and counts, tester, environment, dates, prerequisites, test data, the steps with their results and comments, the screenshots (optional) and lines for the names, dates and signatures of the tester and the approver. The protocol reads in the document language; the toolbar above it follows the interface language and is not printed.

## Beside Business Central

**Run beside Business Central** on the test page opens the run in the browser's side panel next to the open Business Central tab (`src/ui/test-panel.html`), preferring a tab in the tested environment. The panel shows one step at a time with its expected result, the result choices, a comment and the step's screenshots. Choosing Passed or Skipped moves to the next step without a result; Failed stays on the step so that the tester can describe what happened. Previous, Next and Go to step move freely. The browser opens a panel only straight from a click, so the page looks up the Business Central tab beforehand; with no tab open it says so.

The page and the panel change the same stored run. Each sends only the fields that changed (`T9_UPDATE_TEST_RUN`), the background applies the changes to one run one at a time, and each page shows a change made in the other through storage while keeping its own changes that are still waiting to be saved.

## Screenshots

**Take screenshot** stores a picture of the Business Central tab with the step, up to ten per step. In the panel it is the tab shown beside it; on the test page that tab is shown for the moment of the capture and the page is shown again afterwards. Values on the page are measured as in a recording. The browser captures a tab only once the user has used the extension on it (`activeTab`), for example by choosing its toolbar button while the Business Central tab is shown; site access alone is not enough, and opening the popup from code does not count. Until then the capture fails with a message that says so (`test.screenshotNeedsAccess`), and the access lasts while the tab stays open on Business Central.

The test whose page or panel was opened last is the active test (`t9_active_test_run`). The toolbar popup on a Business Central tab shows it at the top, with its progress and **Continue test**, as long as it has steps not yet tested; it is not offered during a recording. **Continue test** opens it in the panel, and because it starts from the toolbar button, screenshots of that tab work without a further step. **End test** stops offering it (`T9_CLEAR_ACTIVE_TEST_RUN`, which clears the pointer only if it still names that test); the run and its results are kept, and opening the test again makes it active again.

Opening the popup on a Business Central tab is remembered for the browser session (`t9_test_access_tabs` in session storage) until the tab closes or leaves Business Central. On a tab where a test runs without that, the toolbar button gets a `!` that blinks a few times and then stays, with a tooltip saying what to do, and the panel shows the same instruction above the step (when the button is not pinned to the toolbar, `chrome.action.getUserSettings`, the instruction points to the browser’s Extensions menu instead and suggests pinning it, since the mark is not seen there); both go away when the popup is opened on the tab. A capture refused by the browser removes the tab from the list again. The mark is not set while recording, and clearing it gives the tab the button's own badge back. A screenshot can be opened full size or deleted. Screenshots are stored under `t9_test_shot_<recording id>:<test run id>:<screenshot id>` (`TEST_SCREENSHOT_PREFIX`), belong to the tested document in library export and sync, and are deleted with the document. **Run again** starts without screenshots.

## Recording a test

**Start the test** in the panel records Business Central while the tester works through the test, in the Business Central tab shown beside the panel, and compares the recording with the test's steps while it is recorded: shortly after the tester acts (at most once every 1.2 seconds, `scheduleLiveTestCheck`), the recording so far is interpreted and compared as described below. A step the recording shows done is set to **Passed according to the recording**; a step Business Central showed an error after is set to **Failed according to the recording**, with Business Central's message added to its comment. The panel follows: it shows the next step without a result after a passed step, and the failed step after an error, with a short status message and without moving the focus; it also says how many steps the recording has shown so far. **Finish the test** (or stopping from the toolbar button, which then asks for no document name) makes the last comparison, adds the screenshots and says how many steps passed and failed according to the recording.

A result the recording set (`resultSource: "recording"`, with the message it added as `recordingError`) is labelled as such on the pages, in the exported files and in the test protocol, and it counts as passed or failed. Only steps without a result of the tester's own are set; choosing a result makes it the tester's own, and the recording leaves it. A result the recording set follows the latest comparison: a step a later comparison no longer finds is not tested again and the message it added is taken out of the comment; a comment the tester wrote stays. If a comparison while recording fails, the panel says so and the recording goes on; the test is compared when it is finished. Per step the latest comparison is also kept as before (**Done according to the recording**, **Not found in the recording**, **Cannot be compared with the recording**, with the recorded instruction), and the panel says how many recorded steps are not in the test. Runs compared by an earlier version keep their suggestions, and **Approve all done steps** still passes those that have no result.

Comparison (`src/document/test-recording-match.js`): each test step keeps a signature of the documented step when the run is created (`signature`: the kind of action, page object id and caption, control id, field and action captions), taken from the step's interaction or, for a step the document's rules rewrote, from its semantic action (its `actionType` and `targetField`). The recording is interpreted as the document library interprets a recording, with the knowledge repository, and with secrets masked as in a bug report. Its steps are paired with the test's steps in order: a page or control id decides when both have one, captions (without case or spacing) are used when an id is missing; ids come from the Business Central knowledge and can differ between the document and the test, so ids that differ with the same page name or the same field and action captions lower the score instead of ruling the pair out; and another kind of action on the same field or button lowers the score instead of ruling the pair out, since the same click can be interpreted more or less precisely. A record chosen another way is the same step: steps that choose a vendor, customer, item, location or bin match whichever field was used (number or name), and for other fields the number and name of the same thing form one family ("Vendor No." and "Vendor Name", "Leverantörsnr" and "Leverantörsnamn", "N° fournisseur" and "Nom fournisseur", in every registered language). A page is compared by its name (a new record's page, "Ny - Inköpsorder", has the same name): the order or record shown in a document page's caption ("Inköpsorder - 2600074 ∙ Exempelleverantören"), a company in parentheses and the browser's " - Dynamics 365 Business Central" are left out, since a test uses other records. Opening the same page is the same step whatever was typed in the search and wherever it started: by object id, or by the page the search opened (the recorded step's navigation outcome, kept as `openedPage`, or else the last caption the step's instruction names). Older documents wrote a search as three steps (the search, the text typed in Business Central's search box and the result chosen in the list of results); right after a found search, those two parts are done with it, and the recorded search is listed with the first. A step that chooses something and a step that chooses or enters something with the same number of three or more digits are the same step, such as item 30043 picked from a list in the document and searched for in the test; a number in the page caption does not count. **Show what the recording held** lists every recorded step with the test step it was paired with (`recordingCheck.recorded`).

Screenshots and errors: each step found in the recording gets the last screenshot of the recorded step, with the values measured when it was taken, stored as a test screenshot marked `source: "recording"`; a new check replaces those and keeps the tester's own, within the limit of ten per step. While a test is recorded the content script captures Business Central errors as during a bug recording (error dialogs as error evidence, error banners on the page). A step whose recorded action was followed by an error is suggested as **failed** with Business Central's message as written (or a note that the message could not be read); **Fail the step with the error message** sets the result and adds the message to the comment once, and **Approve all done steps without errors** passes only steps suggested as done. Values may differ, since a test often uses other data, and ids do not depend on the language Business Central is shown in. Tests created before this version have no signatures and say that the test must be created again from the document to be recorded; **Run again** keeps the signatures.

The recording is not a document: it is linked to the run (`testRunId` on the recording), never listed in the library, not exported or counted in usage statistics, and deleted once the run keeps what it showed (`recordingSuggestion` per step, `recordingCheck` on the run). If the comparison fails, the recording is kept, still hidden, and **Try comparing again** retries it; it is deleted with the tested document. A new check replaces the previous one, and **Run again** starts without suggestions.

## Test suites

A test suite runs the tests of several documents together, for example as the regression test before a Business Central upgrade. In the document library, select the documents and choose **Create test suite**; give the suite a name, the environment and the Business Central version. A test run is made for each document as **Run test** makes it (the environment and version are written in the run's environment); a document that cannot become a test, such as a bug report, is left out and named. The suite's page opens.

The suite's page (`test-suite.html`) shows the suite's result and how many tests are run to the end and how many failed, and per test its status (not started, in progress, passed, failed) and how many steps have a result. **Open test** opens the run on its own page, which links back to the suite; the suite page follows the runs as they change. Name, environment and version are saved automatically. **New round** runs the same tests again in a new suite that names the previous one, for example after the next upgrade: each test gets a new run with the expected results, prerequisites and test data carried over, and nothing tested. **Delete suite** asks on the page and deletes only the suite; its runs stay with their documents as earlier runs. A test whose document was deleted is shown as such and is not counted. The suites are listed above the documents in the library while nothing is searched.

The model is `src/document/test-suite.js`: a suite (`schemaVersion` 1, stored under `t9_test_suite_<id>`, `TEST_SUITE_PREFIX`) holds its title, environment, version, `previousSuiteId` and one item per document (`sessionId`, `title`, `testRunId`); the runs name their suite (`suiteId`). A suite never sets a result: its progress is counted from the runs (`progress`). Unknown fields are kept and an unknown schema version is refused. A suite is exported and synchronized with one of its documents, its owner (`ownerSessionId`, the first document when the suite is made; `library-transfer.js` reads it from the stored value). When the owner document is deleted, the first other document of the suite still in the library becomes the owner (`withoutOwner`); a suite with no document left is deleted with the last one. The deleted document's test stays in the suite, shown as missing. Exporting only some documents takes along the suites they own; a test whose document is not imported shows as missing on the other computer.

**Test protocol** on the suite's page opens the protocol page for the whole suite (`test-protocol.html?suiteId=`): the suite's result, environment, version and creation date, an overview with each test's result and step counts (a test whose document was deleted is listed as such), then each test's own protocol on a new printed page, and one set of signatures for the suite. Each test reads in the language of its run; the suite's heading and overview in the language of its first run. Screenshots are left out until **Include screenshots** is chosen, and are then read run by run.

## Bug report from a failed step

**Create bug report from this step** is offered on a failed step once the tester has described what happened. The report gets a recording of its own without events and holds the document's steps up to the failed one as the user's reproduction steps, the step's expected result and the tester's description as the actual result, and `source` naming the test run and step. The step's screenshots go with the report as its screenshots, with the measured values, so the report covers values the way it does for a recording. The step then links to the report. Nothing is invented: the texts are the document's and the user's own.

## Storage

Each run is stored under `t9_test_run_<id>` (`TEST_RUN_PREFIX`) and names the recording it tests (`sessionId`). Runs use `schemaVersion` 1; unknown fields are kept and an unknown schema version is refused without changing the stored run. Deleting a document deletes its test runs; bug reports made from them are kept. Nothing is sent outside the browser.
